# A call site binds one two-way prop and leaves another unbound: `:a` writes
# the caller's `x`, and `b` is a cell of the instance that starts at 5
# (design/instances.md, *A two-way prop the caller leaves unbound*). A test
# reads each through the instance: the unbound one is the cell, and the bound
# one what its call site bound, `c.x` -- which every compiled target refused
# to name (`c.pA undefined` on Go, `undefined` on html), the read being left
# for a node's own prop.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component pair(:a int, :b int) ui.node {
    ui.vbox {
        ui.button #incA(text="a {a}", @click {
            a = a + 1
        })
        ui.button #incB(text="b {b}", @click {
            b = b + 10
        })
    }
}

component main ui.node {
    var x = 1
    ui.vbox {
        pair #p(:a=x, b=5)
        ui.text #shown(value="x {x}")
    }
}

func testOneBoundOneNot(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.p.incA.click()
    c.p.incB.click()
    t.assert(c.x == 2)
    t.assert(c.p.a == 2)
    t.assert(c.p.b == 15)
    c.x = 7
    t.assert(c.p.a == 7)
}

ui.window {
    main
}
